results.reason: Issue 1 says MSA §3.2 covers all warehousing, freight and delivery services throughout the United States, contrasts this with TS §4.1's NYC-metro last-mile limit, and gives a redline narrowing exclusivity to last-mile in the Service Area.

Issues 2 and 3 say §11.3 carves out only Customer's §10.2 indemnity, leaving it uncapped while Provider's §10.1 indemnity stays under the 12-month cap. They call this one-way exposure and recommend making the carve-outs symmetrical, with a fault-based §10.2.

Issue 6 identifies DPA §9.1's Delaware law and Wilmington courts, notes the conflict with MSA §18.1 and TS §11 (New York), says the DPA comes first under MSA §2.3, and recommends conforming the DPA to MSA §18.
Issue 4 covers §14.2's 3-year auto-renewals and the 15-day window, quantifies the lock-in cost, and recommends 1-year renewals, a 60-day notice period and a reminder notice from Provider.

Issue 5 says SOW §8.2 lets Provider assign without consent while MSA §17.4 restricts only Customer. It notes the risk of transfer to an unknown, unrated or competitor-owned entity and recommends mutual consent plus deleting §8.2.
The memo says MSA §2.3 puts the DPA first. Its proposed redline and its statement that the MSA is above the SOW show the order DPA, then MSA, then SOW.
Issue 3 states the cap is 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim' (MSA §11.1).
The document is a memorandum addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue gives the location ('Where'), 'Why it matters', and a recommendation.
Part 2 is headed 'Issues in Order of Importance' with severity labels, and Part 4 lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The memo concludes that the DPA overrides the MSA on data disputes and treats the governing-law clauses as inconsistent.
The memo describes the exclusivity clause as far broader than the Term Sheet and a direct departure from it.
